text:
alex: Heads up — after last night's kernel rollout i'm seeing a p99 token-latency spike on /api/v1/generate. This started ~10m after deploy. Paging if needed :rotating_light:

deploy-bot: Deploy finished: kernel-service v2.4.1 -> prod @ 2026-03-07T02:13:20Z (rollout 100%)

jia: Confirmed on dashboard. p50 ~ stable, p95 small increase, but p99 jumped from ~120ms -> ~560ms for that route around 02:23 UTC.

sam: I'll pull token-level telemetry and KV stats. Initial hunch: new kernel selection + batching heuristics changed cache locality and increased KV misses.

sam: Querying token-level hist and kv rates now:
```promql
sum by(route) (histogram_quantile(0.99, rate(token_latency_seconds_bucket[5m])))
rate(kv_cache_misses_total{route="/api/v1/generate"}[5m]) / (rate(kv_cache_hits_total{route="/api/v1/generate"}[5m]) + 1e-9)
```

marie: ops-bot paged oncall at 1769532200 — severity: page (p99 > 500ms for 3 consecutive 5m windows).

ops-bot: Pager: paging oncall-pager (sam). Incident severity: page. Route: /api/v1/generate. Condition: token_p99 > 0.5s.

sam: Got the page, looking at traces. Kernel selection traces show a ~60% increase in fallback kernel execution for long sequences which hits a slower matmul path. Also seeing KV miss ratio jump 4x for that route. Attaching small profile excerpt:
```
profile-summary: kernel_select: 32% (was 12%), matmul_slow_path: 28% (was 10%), kv_lookup: 14% (was 4%)
median_batch_size: dropped from 12 -> 6, tail small-batches increased
```

jia: That matches metrics: batching histogram shifted left (more small batches) and KV eviction rate spiked after roll due to TTL and slightly different key layout from kernel variant.

alex: Options: 1) rollback kernel -> restores baseline but costs time, 2) tweak alerting to avoid more noisy pages, 3) tune KV ttl/evict and batching heuristics live. Thoughts? :thinking_face:

marie: My recommendation: avoid immediate rollback. First try live config fixes and alert tuning to stop paging on transient churn. I'll take ownership of adjusting alert thresholds and burn-rate window.

jia: I can push two dynamic flag changes: increase kv_ttl for that route from 30m -> 60m and bump batcher.min_batch_wait from 5ms -> 8ms to reduce small-batch churn. Both are dynamic flags (no restart). Will push in 2m and monitor.

alex: Do those require a restart?

jia: No, we have a config API. Will stage to 10% then 100% if green.

deploy-bot: Flag update: kv_ttl=60m applied for route=/api/v1/generate by jia @1769532320

sam: After kv_ttl + batcher tweak (rolled to 100%) p99 dropped to ~210ms in the 5m window. KV miss rate down ~3x. Still above baseline but big improvement. Monitoring for 30m. :chart_with_upwards_trend:

marie: I'm updating the SLO alert rule to reduce noise during rollouts. New temporary rule proposal:
```yaml
alert: HighTokenLatencyPage
expr: histogram_quantile(0.99, rate(token_latency_seconds_bucket[10m])) > 0.6
for: 10m
labels:
  severity: page
annotations:
  runbook: https://redwood/ops/runbooks/kernel-rollout-latency
```
I'll push to staging then prod after 5m green.

ops-bot: Incident created: IR-2026-042 (kernel-rollout-tailspike). Assignees: sam, jia, alex.

alex: Good. Capture these action items for postmortem: kernel variant differences (kernel selector), batching histograms, kv eviction pattern, and the alerting burn-rate/window tuning. Tag eng-runtime + eng-sre.

sam: Will collect traces and a small perf diff (before/after kv_ttl+bump). I'll upload profiles to the incident ticket.

marie: I'll revert the temporary alert window once 48h stable. For now paging threshold bumped to 600ms and for window 10m.

oncall-pager: Acknowledged. Monitoring continues.

sam: Closing loop for now — p99 stable ~200ms for last 15m. If p99 climbs again i'll reopen incident. Thanks team :heart:
